procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: continues treatment at the cancer center every few weeks. Daughter drives. Pain mostly in the right hip now, worse late in the day. Uses IR morphine once or twice daily on top of the ER. Bowels ok. Tired on treatment weeks. Eating maybe half of what she used to, mostly rice and soup.
No falls. No new back pain, no leg weakness.

Exam: thin, NAD. Lungs clear, heart regular. Port site clean. Right hip tender laterally, ROM limited by pain. Walks with cane.

A/P
- Metastatic breast cancer, bone - on oncology's regimen.
- Cancer pain - acceptable per her; plan and refills with oncology.
- Poor intake, weight drifting down - asked her to mention it to oncology; they may want to add something for appetite. Daughter will bring a 3-day food log next time.
RTC 3 months, annual wellness visit.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Fill history update
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fill report shows new Rx: mirtazapine 15 mg, 1 tab at bedtime, #30, filled 3/9, prescriber oncology. No letter from oncology. Called daughter: yes, oncologist started it for appetite and sleep. Added to med list as outside med. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Seen. Reasonable choice. No interacting meds on our list. Will review at April visit.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, with daughter.
Weight continues down, 4 kg since October. Oncology started mirtazapine 15 mg at night in March for appetite; she thinks she sleeps better, appetite a little better, not much. Food log: rice, instant noodles, tea, some fruit. Little protein. Rarely outside now beyond appointments.
Function: needs help with shopping and cleaning now, still bathes and dresses herself. No falls. Husband home with her.
PHQ-2 1. Says she is sad sometimes about the cancer but not depressed.
Cognition: clock and recall normal.
Health care proxy: daughter, form on file.

Exam: cachectic, temporal wasting. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Right hip tender. Uses cane.

A/P
1. Cancer anorexia-cachexia - added to problem list. On mirtazapine per oncology. Protein with every meal, oral supplement drinks between meals; daughter to stock them.
2. Metastatic breast ca to bone, cancer pain, opioid constipation - unchanged, oncology managing.
3. Labs today.
Vaccines current. Screening deferred given active metastatic disease. RTC 3 months.

orders.reason: proximal weakness and diffuse bone pain, question of metabolic bone disease

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - fatigue and weakness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, aching all over, can't get out of a chair.
S: Over 6-8 weeks, more fatigue and a deep ache in the shins and arms, different from her hip pain. Last few weeks needs to push off with both hands to stand from a chair and pull on the rail for stairs. No new focal back pain. Bowels ok. Oncology says her treatment is going about as expected.

O: Thin. Hip flexors and deltoids 4/5 bilaterally, distal strength normal. Rises from chair only with arms. Bones of the lower legs and forearms tender to pressure. Reflexes symmetric. Sensation intact.

A/P: Proximal weakness with diffuse bone tenderness away from her known metastatic sites. Could be disease, but the pattern and her diet and limited time outdoors make a metabolic bone problem worth looking for. Referral to endocrinology; asked them to see her soon. Let oncology know. Return sooner if new back pain, leg numbness or trouble with bladder/bowel.

conditions.label: Sarcopenia
conditions.note: secondary to malignancy and vitamin D deficiency

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule (50,000 units) by mouth once weekly
medications.reason: severe vitamin D deficiency; prescribed by endocrinology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily with meals

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/17/2023
Reason: fatigue, generalized bone discomfort, difficulty standing from seated. Referred by primary care.

HPI: 66-year-old woman with stage IV right breast IDC metastatic to bone, on palliative therapy with her oncologist, seen for fatigue, aching bones and new trouble getting up from a chair over the past two months. Her diet is mostly rice and instant noodles and she seldom gets outdoors.

Medications: morphine ER 30 mg q12h, morphine IR 15 mg q4h prn, senna 8.6 mg bid, docusate 100 mg bid, prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn, mirtazapine 15 mg qhs.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
Family history: mother breast cancer at 55 (deceased); maternal aunt ovarian cancer; father hypertension.
Social: retired textile worker, never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: thin woman. Weakness of the proximal muscles in arms and legs. Both tibias and both forearms are tender when pressed. Gait is wide-based. Mild kyphosis.

Labs today: calcium 7.3 mg/dL, phosphate 1.9 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 230 U/L, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 6 ng/mL, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D undetectable.
DXA: bone mineral density decreased, pattern consistent with osteomalacia.

Impression:
1. Severe vitamin D deficiency with osteomalacia.
2. Hypocalcemia from the above; phosphate also low.
3. Sarcopenia, from her malignancy and vitamin D deficiency together.

Plan:
- Cholecalciferol 50,000 units by mouth once weekly.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg by mouth three times daily with meals.
- Dietary counseling given: dairy or fortified soy, fish, eggs; daylight exposure as able.
- Recheck calcium, phosphorus and 25-hydroxyvitamin D in about 3 months; primary care may draw.
- Will copy oncology.

Thank you for this referral.

orders.reason: 3-month recheck on vitamin D and calcium

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after endo. Read their letter: vitamin D 6, calcium 7.3, phos 1.9, ALP 230, osteomalacia on DXA. Now on cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly and calcium carbonate 600 mg with each meal. Taking both; daughter set up a pill box. The calcium tablets are large, she cuts them in half.
Says the shin aching is a little less already. Still pushes up from chairs.

Exam: vitals ok. Proximal weakness unchanged. No Chvostek. Lungs clear.

A/P
- Vitamin D deficiency with osteomalacia, hypocalcemia, sarcopenia: added to list, endo plan in place. Recheck Ca/phos/vit D late October, I'll draw here.
- Calcium is better tolerated split with meals; ok to keep cutting tablets.
- Flu/COVID in September.
RTC after the October labs.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose influenza and 2023-24 COVID vaccine, left deltoid, between treatment cycles. Pt in wheelchair from the car today for the long hallway, walks short distances with cane. No reactions.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Venipuncture left arm (no right arm draws). Tolerated.

documents.title: Vitamin D and calcium results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: vitamin D is up from 6 to 22, calcium from 7.3 to 8.7 and phosphorus from 1.9 to 2.9. Moving the right way. Keep taking the weekly vitamin D and the calcium with meals. I'm sending a copy to endocrinology.

documents.title: RE: Vitamin D and calcium results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (daughter) Thank you! She says her legs ache less. Should she keep the same dose forever?

documents.title: RE: Vitamin D and calcium results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: For now yes, same doses. We'll recheck at her spring physical and go from there.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check. Daughter here. Treatment continues at the cancer center; per pt oncologist pleased enough. Hip pain stable on the morphine. Bone aching in the legs much less since vitamin D. Still weak getting up but better than summer. Weight down another 2 kg. Eats more with the mirtazapine than before, still small portions.

Exam: cachectic. Lungs clear, heart regular. Proximal strength 4/5, rises with arm push. Right hip tender. Port ok.

A/P
1. Hypocalcemia - resolved on October labs; removing from list. Recheck CMP today.
2. Vitamin D deficiency/osteomalacia - continue current doses, vitamin D level at April AWV.
3. Cachexia/sarcopenia - continue supplements and mirtazapine. Offered home PT; prefers to wait.
4. Metastatic breast cancer - per oncology.
RTC April AWV.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Health risk review with pt and daughter. Needs help with shopping, cooking and cleaning; husband and daughter share these. Bathes with a shower chair. No falls since last year. Uses cane indoors, wheelchair for longer distances.
PHQ-2 1. Cognition intact on screen. Hearing/vision ok.
Advance care: proxy is daughter. Talked briefly about what matters most to her; she wants to be home and to see her family's events. Not ready yet for a full goals-of-care conversation, would like to come back to it.

Exam: cachectic, alert. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Right hip tender. Proximal weakness unchanged.

Plan:
- Vitamin D level today.
- Personalized plan given: protein intake, supplements, home exercise sheet for sit-to-stand.
- RSV vaccine in the fall with flu and COVID.
- Routine cancer screening not indicated given metastatic disease.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Vitamin D result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vitamin D is 31 now, in the normal range. Keep going as you are.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Daughter called to cancel 6/11, mother has an infusion that day that was moved. Will call back to reschedule after her July oncology visit.

documents.title: Medical oncology follow-up, July 2024
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 07/29/2024

Interval history: Ms. Zhang, 67, with stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast metastatic to bone, continues palliative systemic therapy. Since her last visit she has more fatigue and is finding it harder to keep up with daily tasks. Her granddaughter graduates at an outdoor ceremony in about three months and she very much wants to be there; she worries she will not have the stamina. She feels well supported at home. Endocrinology saw her last summer for weakness and bone aches.

Medications: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg q12h; morphine sulfate IR 15 mg q4h prn breakthrough pain; cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly; calcium carbonate 600 mg tid with meals; senna 8.6 mg bid; docusate 100 mg bid; prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn nausea; mirtazapine 15 mg qhs.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Vitals stable. Exam: cachectic. Diffuse tenderness over bone.

Labs: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, calcium 10.5 mg/dL, albumin 3.0 g/dL.

Assessment/Plan: Metastatic breast cancer to bone on palliative therapy, with fatigue and declining function. Continue current treatment. Discussed pacing and rest before the graduation; wheelchair for the event. No medication changes. Return in 6-8 weeks.

(Sent at the request of the primary care office.)

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from June. Saw oncology 7/29. Per pt and daughter: more tired, treatment continues, "blood a little low", no med changes. Her goal is her granddaughter's graduation this fall, outdoors; wants to be well enough to sit through it.
Tired most afternoons. Pain about the same. Eating small amounts. Bowels ok.

Exam: cachectic, in wheelchair today. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Diffuse bony tenderness, worst right hip.

A/P
- Metastatic breast ca/bone, fatigue - per oncology. We do not have the July note; front desk to request it.
- Graduation planning: pace the day, rest beforehand, IR morphine before leaving the house, wheelchair, shade and water. She liked that plan.
- Vit D/calcium - continue.
RTC after flu shots / early winter.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Second request to the cancer center for the 7/29 oncology note (first request faxed 8/13). They have no record of the fax. Re-faxed with signed release. Was told 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high dose), 2024-25 COVID and RSV given, left arm x2 and left thigh. Pt in wheelchair. Daughter says the graduation is in 2 weeks and they have a plan. No reactions.
